item.title: Blaschke--Santal\'o inequalities with respect to costs
item.description: arXiv:2610.19085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study functional Blaschke--Santal\'o inequalities in which the inner product is replaced by a cost. An inequality on each orthant, combined with Steiner symmetrization, gives a sufficient condition for a cost inequality to hold for even convex functions. We apply this principle to a multiplicative cost defined on all orthants. Its second variation gives a weighted improvement of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality in the directions for which differentiation is justified. We also prove an $L^p$ version of the Fradelizi--Meyer theorem from a weighted volume-product inequality and derive the corresponding radial cost and Brascamp--Lieb inequalities. Explicit examples include anisotropic power and Cauchy densities, with dilation equality cases and a sharp obstruction below the coordinate exponent two. For the spherical logarithmic cost we compute an exact entropy--logdet deficit decomposition and the second-order deficit transverse to ellipsoids. We also explain the transport-entropy formulation and distinguish the restricted spectral question from the scalar $(B)$ property.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Kolesnikov, Galyna V. Livshyts, Liran Rotem

item.title: Orthogonal partition by four hyperplanes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$. The threshold coincides with the geometric lower bound precisely when $m=2^j-1$. Consequently, $\Delta^*(2^j-1,4,3)=7\cdot2^{j-1}-2$ for every $j\geq1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Fakhrutdinov, Platon Khamatov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: A short open space curve of unit width
item.description: arXiv:2610.19585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Tinko Sebastian Bartels, Dennis Kevin Choy, Ruixiang Wu, Tongxin Li

item.title: Strong Negative Type of Star-shaped Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metric spaces of negative type (NT) and strong negative type (SNT) are fundamental in wide applications across computer science and statistics. It is well-known that spheres equipped with geodesic distance are of NT, and subsets of a sphere that contain at most one pair of antipodal points (e.g. an open hemisphere) are of SNT. In this paper, we extend these results to a class of star-shaped manifolds. By constructing a metric $d$ based on layer-wise radial projections, we prove that every star-shaped manifold, equipped with $d$, is of NT. Moreover, we prove that a subset of a star-shaped manifold is of SNT under certain injectivity and directional asymmetry conditions. In particular, for a subset of a single layer, it is of SNT if it contains exactly one point from each preimage of an open hemisphere (a fully directional asymmetry); moreover, it is of SNT if and only if it contains at most one opposite-directional pair.
item.dc:creator: Hang Liu, Ziyan Xu

item.title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.19253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $\pi$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Berkani

item.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.19664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Amp\`ere potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.
item.dc:creator: Erxiao Wang

item.title: New spherical codes by tuning an annealing solver
item.description: arXiv:2610.19988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spherical code problem asks how to place $N$ points on a unit sphere in $D$ dimensions to maximize the smallest distance between two points. It is a non-smooth and non-convex max-min problem, where few problem sizes have known optimal solutions, some have constructions, but most still only have numerically obtained solutions. We use a simple solver, with seven parameters, that anneals a LogSumExp surrogate, minimizes with L-BFGS, applies a random perturbation between anneals, and repeats with no acceptance test until a fixed limit is reached. We search the solver parameters for every instance with $N \le 1024$, $3 \le D \le 32$, and $N > 2D$, a total of 29,670 instances, using 32 parameter trials. We then run the solver for 60 seconds with the best parameters for each instance, without utilizing any symmetries or existing solutions. After enforcing monotonicity of the results and numerically polishing the solutions, we improve the best known code in 4,577 instances. When a single set of solver parameters is used for all instances, with one 60-second episode, the number of improvements is still 3,649. From our records, we find 24 codes with an exact algebraic cosine. Among our ablations, we find that 1) the repeated anneal contributes most to improvements, 2) at our $32 \times 60$-second budget only fitting one parameter per-instance is better than fitting all seven, and 3) good parameters can be predicted from the instance size. We provide the solver code, the fitted parameters, and the codes.
item.dc:creator: Ilmari Vahteristo

item.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Connected p.c.f self-similar fractals satisfying the angle separation condition have conformal dimension 1
item.description: arXiv:2303.10320v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let ${\mathcal G}$ be a graph-directed iterated function system (GIFS) satisfying the finite post-critical points property (p.c.f), and assume that the attractors $(M_\ell)_{\ell\in{\mathcal L}}$ are connected. In this paper, we use valuation pairs to construct new metrics on the attractor of ${\mathcal G}$, which seems to be very natural but yet is not seen in literature. Surprisingly, under these new metrics, the GIFS becomes nearly self-similar. Moreover, we show that, if the original GIFS is self-similar and satisfies an angle separation condition, then for every $\ell\in {\mathcal L}$, $(M_\ell,d_\ell)$ is symmetrically equivalent to $(M_\ell,D_\ell)$, where $d_\ell$ is the original metric and $D_\ell$ is the induced metric. Consequently, the conformal dimension of $M_\ell$ is $1$ for every $\ell\in {\mathcal L}$.
item.dc:creator: Hui Rao, Zhi-Ying Wen, Qihan Yuan

item.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.13972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A unit ball is surrounded with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders. Each cylinder touches the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more cylinder of the same radius be added if the configuration may be rearranged? Can the $n$ cylinders instead be enlarged, and by how much? We prove that insertion is impossible for $3\le n\le7$ and possible for $n\ge9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$ is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, which was resolved recently. We prove that the ring of four cylinders cannot be expanded. This settles a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman from 2018. For $n\ge5$ the largest possible expansion radius remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.14236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipschitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Fotis Ioannidis, Vyron Vellis

item.title: Angles and volumes of simplices, boxes, and crosspolytopes in constant curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.21571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine, up to isometry, the Riemannian tangent and normal cones at arbitrary faces of boxes, acute orthocentric simplices, rectangular simplices, and asymmetric crosspolytopes in spaces of constant sectional curvature $\kappa\in\mathbb R$. Using these descriptions, we derive explicit one-dimensional integral formulas for their internal and external angles in arbitrary dimension. In particular, our results cover regular simplices, cubes, and crosspolytopes, the three families of regular polytopes existing in every dimension. We also establish a correspondence between regular simplices and cubes with isometric local cones at corresponding faces, provided their edge-length parameters are suitably matched. Combining our angle formulas with the Poincar\'e relation, we obtain volume formulas for simplices and crosspolytopes in even dimensions. For boxes, we derive volume formulas valid in every dimension. Among the new results are angle formulas for spherical and hyperbolic cubes and crosspolytopes, volume formulas for asymmetric crosspolytopes, and a one-dimensional integral representation for the internal angles of regular crosspolytopes that appears to be new even in the Euclidean case. The formulas involve the standard normal distribution function $\Phi(x)$ and its values at purely imaginary arguments $\Phi(\mathrm{i} x)$. For example, if $d\geq 2$ is even, then the volume of the ideal regular simplex in the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space of curvature $\kappa=-1$ is given by the absolutely convergent integral $$ \frac{\pi^{d/2}} {\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{i}^{d}\, \Gamma\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left[ \Phi\left(\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} + \Phi\left(-\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} \right] \mathrm{e}^{-y^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}y. $$
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko, Philipp Schange
